title: On Avoiding the busiest street at noon
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：avoid　|　正文 355 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 avoid 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the foreman ① avoided the busiest street at noon for the whole place, and every worker in the site said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the foreman ② avoids the busiest street at noon without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ avoid the busiest street at noon at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ avoided the busiest street at noon before — a line in the sheet for May 1987 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Avoiding the busiest street at noon for the whole place, the foreman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ avoid an argument about nothing without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Avoid an argument about nothing at once and never mention it again.

By 2000 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the sheet, and a new worker from the next site ⑧ avoids an argument about nothing for the whole place every shift without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ramp, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ avoided the busiest street at noon again when nobody else would.

⑩ To avoid the busiest street at noon, my mother said in 2005, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the site remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the site forgets, somebody avoids the busiest street at noon without a word of thanks again and somebody must avoid the busiest street at noon for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 避开（一般过去式 avoided the busiest street at noon：1993 年工头头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 避开（一般现在 avoids the busiest street at noon：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 避开（不定式 to avoid the busiest street at noon：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 避开（过去完成时 had avoided the busiest street at noon：1987 年五月的施工单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 避开（动名词 avoiding the busiest street at noon 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 避免（avoid an argument about nothing：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去避免一场毫无来由的争吵）
G. v. 避免（avoid an argument about nothing：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 避开（后段两处：新来的工人照例 avoids an argument about nothing，而母亲又一次 avoided the busiest street at noon）

answers.why: avoid 意为“避开”，1993 年工头替所有人避开正午最热闹的那条街，那是工地里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 avoided。
avoid 意为“避开”，自那以后工头不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 avoids。
avoid 意为“避开”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯避开正午最热闹的那条街”，此处为不定式 to avoid the busiest street at noon。
avoid 意为“避开”，施工单里 五月 那行字说明早在 2000 年之前就有人避开过，故用过去完成时 had avoided。
avoid 意为“避开”，工头说“避开正午最热闹的那条街这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 avoiding the busiest street at noon 作主语。
avoid 意为“避免”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去避免一场毫无来由的争吵”，should ever 之后用原形 avoid an argument about nothing。
avoid 意为“避免”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻避免一场毫无来由的争吵（avoid an argument about nothing at once），以后再也不要提起。
avoid 意为“避开”，新来的工人每个班次都照例避免一场毫无来由的争吵，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 avoids。
avoid 意为“避开”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人避开正午最热闹的那条街，用一般过去式 avoided 叙述。
avoid 意为“避开”，结尾那句是母亲 2005 年的话：要避开正午最热闹的那条街，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工地记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 avoid 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the foreman avoided the busiest street at noon for the whole place, and nobody in the site forgot it.
Even now the foreman avoids the busiest street at noon without a word of thanks whenever the site asks.
Avoiding the busiest street at noon for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever avoid an argument about nothing without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next site avoids an argument about nothing for the whole place every shift, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother avoided the busiest street at noon again, and the site remembered that half.
